# Day-84 replay of the published OULAD review queue

Frozen before computing queue or ranking metrics from the prediction files. This is a secondary audit of Sánchez Trujillo et al. (2026), DOI 10.3390/data11110281. The published comparator is the assessment logistic regression top-10% capacity policy in Table 7.

- Use the full 2014J temporal test, retaining returning learners as in Table 7. Independently construct the risk set from the pinned UCI OULAD registration and outcome tables. Join by module, presentation and learner. Include observed registration dates through day 84 and exclude unregistrations through day 84, including on that day. The positive endpoint is the archive's final `Withdrawn` category on the eligible roster. Do not infer an administrative date from the outcome. Count raw roster dates and report how many eligible positives lack a dated subsequent exit.
- Verify source table hashes against the author manifest and compare the supplement source with the pinned UCI release. Require exact agreement on keys, dates and outcomes in the day-84 analytical data and on keys, labels and student-disjoint flags across every prediction file. Stop on duplicate or unmatched keys or label discrepancies. Count the published 2014J risk set, positives and disjoint subset against the authors' aggregate files. Use the full shared risk set for all scoring.
- Replay the pooled queue using the highest calibrated probabilities and ceil(roster size / 10) slots. Copy the authors' stable file-order tie rule for the published comparator. Audit cutoff ties and also report expected true positives if cutoff ties are split uniformly. Verify the assessment logistic regression queue against the supplement workload counts and Table 7's precision, recall and per-1,000 figures at published rounding. Report seats, TP, FP, FN, TN, precision and recall for every model. Include uniform selection's expected captures at the same budget.
- Use the frozen assessment LR, RF and XGBoost scores on the same cases. Also include the five published score-free and VLE variants so the best archived day-84 ranking and queue are visible without post-result comparator selection. Report pooled AUC and average precision and verify both against the matching performance rows. Rank queues by captured positives at identical capacity, without fitting or selecting a new model. Differences are descriptive on the reused holdout.
- Inventory the coverage of the saved scores on the day-84 roster and on counterfactual rosters with withdrawal status delayed by 1, 7, 14 and 30 days or unavailable. Keep registration eligibility current. With lag L, admit dated exits after day 84−L along with the active roster. Report the number admitted without scores and the number with final Withdrawn. Treat this as a coverage diagnostic only. Published scores are unavailable for admitted prior exits, so the archival rankings do not identify a stale-roster queue. Do not impute scores or treat retrospective grades as known to staff. Neither reporting latency nor grade release time was observed.
- The day-60 analysis uses a different horizon, risk set and allocation (module budgets). Do not use its precision as a baseline for improvement. Keep inputs and enrollment identifiers outside Git. Save aggregate outputs and reproduce with CPU affinity 0–9.
